title: Microsoft Purview: network DLP policies for all websites through Entra Internet Access
summary: Hold: Microsoft has not stated whether existing policies change on arrival, so the briefing cannot promise that nothing changes without administrator action. The Entra configuration path also skips creating a rule before selecting its action. The roadmap dates and documented licensing routes are supported.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The new scope is admin-opt-in and nothing changes until an administrator creates or edits a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview network DLP all websites default existing policies scope; network data security all websites pricing license default. Read the roadmap, Network Data Security overview, DLP walkthrough and Entra content policy page; none states the new scope's arrival behaviour.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace 'nothing changes until a policy is set' in the summary with 'Microsoft has not stated the default'. Replace the second paragraph's first sentence in Why it matters with 'Microsoft has not stated whether existing policies change scope on arrival; no source says existing behaviour changes.' This also resolves the conflict with Open questions. Keep action review; it does not require a proven opt-in default.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the Adaptive app scopes tab for choosing network DLP destinations.
claims.quote:
Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy.
Select Inline web traffic.
Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list.
Select + Add cloud apps.
Select the Adaptive app scopes tab
claims.fix: The path reaches the right tab but stops before choosing a scope. Set controls[0].ui.path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > app scope', using app scope as the administrator's chosen category. Retain the note that this documents today's choices, not the all-websites option.

Set controls[2].ui.path to 'Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies > + Create Policy > Rules', ending at the documented rules page rather than inventing a button label. claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, At rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Some checklist controls have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Internet Access traffic forwarding profile enabled, a TLS inspection policy'; 'Choose simulation mode or Audit only'; 'filter Activity explorer'; 'Check the GSA traffic logs'. Table: destination scope, network enforcement plane, and Scan with Purview only.
claims.fix: The Before rollout prerequisite-check bullet, At rollout simulation/Audit only bullet, and both After rollout monitoring bullets name controls without rows. No correction should add rows. Narrow those checklist items to advice without directing readers to set or check an unlisted control: 'Plan a test environment that meets the documented GSA prerequisites', 'Pilot the policy before broader deployment', and 'Investigate user reports with the documented Purview and GSA monitoring tools'. Keep the verified factual details in the body.
